decided_by: the plan of docs/stages/stage-1/reasoning_inheritance/REPORT.md section 11 (maintainer reviews of 2026-11-14 UTC: candidates D / M-avg / M-act at D's fixed structure, fixed before any result). Prepared at $0; it authorizes nothing (authorizes, below)
question: At D's structure (28 blocks, hidden 2560, FFN 9728, 32 query / 8 KV heads, 3,215,021,568 parameters), does writing each span's one block from all of the span's teacher blocks do better on eval-set-1 than keeping the span's first block alone (D, direct deletion)?

teacher.lineage: one teacher lineage (AGENTS.md P17.1): every candidate tensor, the calibration statistics, the state-evaluation reference and the evaluation tokenizer and chat template are this checkpoint's

d_checkpoint.group: D (RI-S1): the teacher's blocks at the frozen selection's 28 kept blocks, its embedding, final norm and (tied) LM head
d_checkpoint.on_the_pod: never moved: each candidate is built from the teacher (frozen_mapping.keep_blocks, D's own builder) and every tensor outside the six span blocks is compared with D's per-tensor digests bit for bit

spans.rule: each removed block joins the nearest kept block before it; the merged block stands where its span starts and receives the span's input; a run of consecutive removed blocks joins as a whole and is merged in one step, never pairwise in sequence (layer_merge.spans_from_kept_blocks on the frozen selection's kept blocks)
spans.anchor: the span's first (kept) block; every absorbed block is aligned onto it
spans.unchanged: the other 22 kept blocks, the embedding, the final norm and the tied LM head: D's, bit for bit

D.evaluation: RI-S1's sealed eval-set-1 records of D, reused, never regenerated

M-avg.role: direct parameter averaging, the merge control
M-avg.formula: for every tensor of a span's blocks (q/k/v/o projections, q_norm, k_norm, gate/up/down projections, input_layernorm, post_attention_layernorm; Qwen3 has no biases): theta' = (1/|span|) * sum_{l in span} theta_l

M-act.role: aligned activation-weighted merging, a heuristic initialization to be tested
M-act.folding: each block's input_layernorm gain into its q/k/v input columns and its post_attention_layernorm gain into its gate/up input columns (W (g * x_hat) = (W diag g) x_hat); the merged block's two gains are 1; q_norm and k_norm act after the projection and are not folded
M-act.alignment: each absorbed block onto the span's anchor: FFN neurons (gate row, up row, down column together) by the linear assignment maximizing the summed Pearson correlation of the gated-product features (the down projection's input); KV groups (each with its 4 query heads) by the linear assignment on the cosine of the groups' summed residual writes; within each matched group the query heads by the linear assignment on the heads' write cosine; q/k/v rows and o_proj columns move together, head dimensions never
M-act.weights: per FFN slot w_{l,i} = s_{l,i} / sum_l s_{l,i}, s = E|a_i| * ||down column i||_2 (ffn.activation_importance_v0's statistic); per query-head slot the head's write energy mean_t ||W_o,h a_h(t)||^2 (attention.activation_importance_v1's statistic); per KV-group slot its 4 heads' summed energy; q_norm / k_norm and the (unit) gains by each block's share of total head energy
M-act.what_it_is_not: the weights are convex per slot. That guarantees neither the scale of the merged block's output nor that it reproduces the teacher span's cumulative update; both are measured (diagnostics) and neither is assumed
M-act.not_part: no least-squares refit, no fitted coefficient, no training: learnable fusion coefficients are Stage 3's

not_registered.parameter_addition: LaCo's theta*_l = theta_l + sum_k (theta_{l+k} - theta_l) has no scaling: on a two-block span it equals keeping the absorbed block instead of the kept one (another deletion, not a merge); summing every tensor doubles the RMSNorm gains, and no primary source gives a scaling rule

candidates.fixed: neither the candidate list nor the decision rule changes after any result is seen; state evaluation and the diagnostics never remove a candidate from generation

statistics.session: the anchor search's own session (driver.session: inputs v3, the packed forward context, the position policy), whose operator config hashes are checked against the journal before anything runs
statistics.positions: the position policy's admitted token positions (positions.supervised_target_v1@v1) of the profile's 558 examples (569,270 tokens before packing; 211,203 admitted), under Stage 1's packing (seeded sha256-keyed shuffle 20261105, sequential packing with truncation into 8,192-token sequences, prefix_restart_v1, causal attention with continuous positions): 79 packed sequences, 644,493 non-padding tokens, 231,242 statistics positions (a fragment's repeated prefix counted like any placement, AGENTS.md P19)

features.ffn: the down projection's input a (the gated product), every neuron
features.heads: the output projection's input per query head a_h, mapped to its residual write W_o,h a_h (2,560-d, the coordinates every block shares)

statistics.where: each block's statistics on its OWN input in the teacher's forward, for the 14 blocks of the six spans
statistics.accumulation: streaming, one packed sequence at a time, from CENTERED moments (layer_merge.PearsonMoments): each sequence's activations centered on their own float64 mean, the centered cross product in float32 at full precision (no TF32) with the exact float64 correction for the rounding of the centered values, merged into float64 means, centered second moments and centered cross moments by Chan, Golub and LeVeque's pairwise update. No difference of two large uncentered sums is taken, so a feature whose spread is small against its mean keeps its variance and its correlations (the earlier E[xy] - E[x]E[y] on float32 sums read a bf16-exact feature at 1000 +/- 4 at an autocorrelation of 0.14; tests/initialization/test_layer_merge.py). Head writes: GramMoments (uncentered by definition: a cosine), float32 per chunk of 1,024 positions, float64 across. Device memory: 8 FFN pairs x 9,728^2 float64 = 6.1 GB beside the 8 GB teacher
statistics.zero_variance: a feature whose variance on the statistics positions is at or below 1e-12 of its mean square (or whose mean square is 0) has correlation 0 with every feature; a head set with zero write energy has cosine 0
statistics.zero_denominator: a slot whose importance (or energy) is 0 in every block of its span takes the uniform weights 1/|span|; the count of such slots is recorded
statistics.assignment: exact maximum-weight perfect matching (layer_merge.linear_assignment: shortest augmenting path with duals, Crouse 2016, the algorithm of scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment), float64; ties: among columns of equal reduced cost an unassigned column first, then the lowest column index
statistics.persisted: records/merge_statistics.safetensors (per block E|a| and head energies; per pair the three permutations) and records/merge_statistics.json (counts, matching quality, digests): pulled to the dev box on the next poll and copied to the relay with the candidates; a later attempt reuses them and never repeats the forward

fold_equivalence.what: every span block with its gains folded, alone, against the unmodified block

permutation_equivalence.what: every absorbed block with its alignment permutation alone, against the unmodified block

checks.rule: float32 copies of the bf16 teacher blocks on every position of the first packed sequence; error ||y' - y||_F / ||y - x||_F (relative to the block's own update; float32 reordering and rounding are about 1e-6 of it). A non-finite error fails the check whatever the others are; exceeding the tolerance is a defect of the mechanism: the build stops before the candidate is saved
checks.unchanged_tensors: every candidate tensor outside the six span blocks equals D's per-tensor digest (d_tensor_digests.json); every span block differs from D's in at least one tensor
checks.structure: each candidate's configuration is D's and its parameter count 3,215,021,568

diagnostics.what: on the statistics positions, for each span: the teacher span's attention update (sum of its blocks' attention outputs), FFN update (sum of their FFN outputs) and whole residual update (span output minus span input), against each of D's, M-avg's and M-act's block run on the same teacher input: RMS norms, norm ratio, cosine and normalized error E|c - r|^2 / E|r|^2 per component
diagnostics.role: diagnostics, like state evaluation: they explain results; they select no candidate, gate no generation and decide nothing

state_eval.role: diagnostic only; both candidates are generated whatever it shows

evaluation.protocol: RI-S1's design.json :: evaluation, unchanged: eval-set-1, every registered unit, both modes, context 40,960 with no token cap, nucleus_v1, seeds from item, turn and sample (each item pairs with D's sealed record), the degeneration check every 256 tokens, the runners at session commit 8f74bc94 (after the abort repair)
evaluation.protocol_sha256_rule: sha256 of json.dumps(RI-S1 design['evaluation'], sort_keys=True); the driver refuses another
evaluation.order_rule: the primary unit of both candidates first, so a budget that ends early leaves the primary comparison measured; the order decides nothing about a result (every item has its fixed seed; a unit is complete or absent)
evaluation.exposure: eval-set-1 is development-exposed; nothing here is an untouched test set, and no per-item result fits a weight, a permutation or a span

analysis.primary: thinking mode (H-T), the static fluid formal core: 570 items, M-avg - D and M-act - D, each item paired with D's sealed record of the same item
analysis.units_of_independence: the registered independence groups (fluid_reasoning_720/independence_v1.json, sha256 4e5a06d48624c14a1eb20aaa5267198b2dfd801d268b7cf13a3f67b8ef17a1c5): the 570 items fall into 558 groups (six groups hold 18 items; every other item is its own group); 708 is the whole fluid unit's count and is not used for the static comparison
analysis.statistic: the item-weighted mean paired difference, delta = (1/570) sum_items (y_M - y_D), y the registered scorer's correctness in {0, 1}; per group g the summed difference d_g
analysis.test: a two-sided paired sign-flip randomization test at the group level: under H0 the M and D labels are exchangeable within every group, so each d_g's sign is flipped independently with probability 1/2; T = |sum_g d_g|; p = (1 + #{b : |sum_g e_bg d_g| >= T}) / (1 + B), B = 100,000 draws of e_bg in {-1, +1} from numpy.random.default_rng(20261114); groups with d_g = 0 contribute nothing and are kept
analysis.direction: two-sided; the sign of delta says better or worse
analysis.multiplicity: Holm over the TWO registered comparisons (M-avg - D, M-act - D) at alpha 0.05, m = 2 always: sort p ascending; adjusted p_(1) = min(1, 2 p_(1)), p_(2) = min(1, max(adjusted p_(1), p_(2))). The family is never shrunk to the candidates that happen to be measured
analysis.decision: only when BOTH candidates' primary units are complete (every registered item has a record): for each candidate BETTER than deletion if its Holm-adjusted p <= 0.05 and delta > 0; WORSE if adjusted p <= 0.05 and delta < 0; NOT DISTINGUISHED otherwise. If either primary unit is not complete there is no test and no verdict for either: each measured candidate is reported descriptively (delta, accuracy and the unadjusted effect interval; status descriptive_only), the other not_measured; never a partial pooling

primary_items.rule: the registered fluid_reasoning_720/dev_v1 items minus the set's formal-core exclusions (eval_set_scoring.unit_masks) minus the interactive episodes; sha256 over the sorted task ids, each followed by a newline. Completeness is checked against this list, never against what a store holds (layer_merge_analysis.registered_primary_items)

analysis.effect_interval: reported beside the test and labeled as such: the percentile 95% interval of delta over 10,000 group-bootstrap resamples (the 558 groups drawn with replacement, delta recomputed as the item-weighted mean; numpy.random.default_rng(20261115)); unadjusted for multiplicity and not the decision
analysis.supplementary: the same interval resampling whole rule families (family_id), as RI-S1 reported; the non-thinking mode, the interactive episodes, each fluid axis, the supporting units, M-act - M-avg; usable rollout and its components; failure types. Reported, never decisive
analysis.resolution: at D's 5.6% static fluid correctness, about 3 pp is roughly the smallest paired difference this design separates from 0 (a rough figure from D's paired discordance, not a power analysis)

products.layout: per candidate, as soon as it is built and its reconstruction verified: <prefix>/<candidate>/<candidate identity sha256[:16]>/delta.safetensors, the six span blocks' 66 tensors (D plus these tensors is the candidate), and for M-act <prefix>/statistics/<statistics identity sha256[:16]>/merge_statistics.safetensors; uploaded from the pod, downloaded again into a fresh cache and re-hashed before the candidate is recorded durable and the next one is built
products.delta_tensor_bytes_rule: the summed tensor bytes of D's span-start blocks (children 2, 9, 14, 20, 23, 24; 66 tensors) in D's model.safetensors header, 1.13 GiB; a candidate's span blocks have D's shapes and dtype
products.reconstruction: lossless: D rebuilt from the teacher (checked against D's 310 tensor digests) with the delta's tensors written in place, saved by the same writer, gives the candidate's artifact digest -- verified on the pod for every candidate, from the delta FILE read back, before it is made durable; a restore that does not give the recorded artifact digest is refused
products.relay_room: checked before the launch at the true sizes (runtime.hub_capacity.would_accept: two deltas of delta_tensor_bytes plus 1 MiB of header each, and the statistics); a refusal stops the launch at $0
products.evidence: every finished file is pulled to the dev box on each poll (<scr>/store), the deltas included (products/<candidate>/delta.safetensors, 1.13 GiB each); records and evaluations about 0.4 GB for two models, from RI-S1's 0.37 GB for three. The resume and evidence archives carry records and evaluations only, never the deltas
products.dev_box_copy: kept: each candidate as D's dev-box copy (protected: the base) plus its pulled delta, 2.3 GiB for both beside D's 6.0 GiB already there. `layer_merge_launch.py retain` re-hashes each delta, rebuilds the candidate's span tensors from D's local file and the delta and compares them with the pod's per-tensor digests, then hard-links it into the out-of-tree store and records it (storage/layer_merge_local.json). No 6.43 GB checkpoint is kept a second time

reuse.never_redone: D's checkpoint and sealed generations; T's reused evaluation; the frozen selection and mapping; the calibration and state-suite items (dev box assets); eval-set-1; RI-S1's runners and the driver's evaluation and resume paths. No corpus is regenerated, no baseline retrained, no valid measurement repeated
reuse.a_failed_attempt: takes over the previous attempt's records and every sealed evaluation part (driver.take_over), and reuses each product only when its recorded identity equals this attempt's (layer_merge_driver.identities: the teacher, the calibration data and its packing and positions, the statistics and merge method and the code computing them, D, the candidate's artifact digest, the evaluation protocol): the statistics and alignments, the checks, each durable candidate (restored from D and its delta, never rebuilt), the diagnostics, each candidate's state evaluation, and per (candidate, mode) the sealed fluid episodes and capability samples -- generating only the items with no sealed record, each under its fixed seed. A product of another identity is moved to superseded/<attempt>/ with the reason and redone; an engineering change outside every identity keeps them all
reuse.per_candidate: each candidate is built, saved, its reconstruction verified, made durable on the relay and registered (records/candidates/<g>.json, status durable) before the next is built, so a failure while the second is built keeps the first. A candidate built and verified but not yet durable (its relay upload or read-back failed) keeps its delta: the dev box's pulled copy goes into the next attempt's resume archive (layer_merge_launch.carried_deltas, re-hashed) and is taken over, so only the relay copy is redone, never the merge. Restoring a durable candidate writes the relay's delta, re-hashed, to the path its record declares (out/products/<g>/delta.safetensors), where the poll pulls it and retain keeps it. The fold and permutation checks are reused only when they PASSED; a failed record of the same identity is kept as evidence and the check is run again
